questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Gift of the gab

options.text: have the talent to speak well

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "have the talent to speak well".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Gift of the gab"** is an idiom that refers to the ability to speak easily and confidently in a way that makes people want to listen to you and believe you.
 
• It denotes the skill of being eloquent and persuasive in speech.
 
 
• For example, in a sentence, it can be used like this: "She's a saleswoman with the gift of the gab, capable of selling sand in a desert."
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer will be **Option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: "**Have the ability to adapt" **is not related to the given idiom.

 
 
• Adaptability is about flexibility and the capacity to adjust oneself readily to different conditions, not specifically about speaking skills.
 
 
 
• Option 2: **"Achieve sudden greatness"** also doesn't align with the idiom.
 
 
• Achieving greatness involves success or distinction in a particular field or endeavor, not necessarily related to speaking.
 
 
 
• Option 4: "**Receive a precious gift"** is a literal interpretation of the idiom but does not reflect the actual figurative meaning of the phrase, which pertains to eloquent and persuasive speaking abilities.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. The fire destroyed many buildings which were rebuilt with red clay tiles.

B. In the year 1689, a huge fire engulfed the city.

C. Prague in the Czech Republic is known for its striking red roofs.

D. Even now, traditional red roofs are included in any repairs or new construction.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. Part CBAD**.
 
• Among the given sentences the independent sentence is C So the answer begins with C.
 
• Second sentence is Part B which as continue the sentence which is C
 
• Sentence B & A make a pair. Sentence B talks about the fire engulfing the city which is continued by sentence A. 
 
• Therefore, the correct sequence is followed by Option 1.

questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

__We are going to have pleasure__ in accepting your kind invitation.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• **The sentence is in simple present tense so the underlined phrase should be in simple present tense.**
 
• 'we are going to have pleasure' is in future continuous tense so this cannot be the answer.
 
• 'we are having pleasure' is in present continuous tense and cannot be the answer.
 
• 'We will have a pleasure' is also wrong because it is in future tense.
 
• **Option 4 'we have pleasure' is in simple present tense and is the most appropriate substitution to the underlined segment.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. This code contains information about its nature.

B. Each living organism has a DNA code.

C. If this genetic material is altered, it would alter the organism.

D. The nature of an individual is determined by the unique genetic material in the code.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. BADC.**
 
• Sentence B explains about the DNA code. Sentence A which begins with 'this code' shows that it is the continuation of the DNA code. So these two sentences make the pair.
 
• Sentence D explains about the genetic material which is continued in the sentence C. So these two sentences make the pair. 
 
• If we begin the sentence with D, it doesn't make a proper sequence after arrangement.
 
• Therefore, the correct sequence is BADC which gives a meaningful sentence after arrangement.

questions.solution:

• case of parallelism is also followed as we can see spilled and began both are in 2nd form of verb as they are joined by conjunction "AND"

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

PROSPERITY
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"prosperity"** means the state of being successful, especially in financial or material terms. (समृद्धि)

 
 
• **Example: **The country's prosperity is evident in its high standard of living and robust economy.
 
 
 
• **"Adversity"** refers to difficulties or misfortune, which is the opposite of prosperity. (विपत्ति)
 
 
• **Example: **She showed great resilience in the face of adversity.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'prosperity'** is **'adversity'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Simplicity** (सरलता): The quality or condition of being easy to understand or do.

 
 
• **Example:** The simplicity of the design makes it very user-friendly.
 
 
 
• **Nobility** (श्रेष्ठता): The quality of being noble in character, mind, birth, or rank.
 
 
• **Example:** His nobility of spirit was evident in his generous actions.
 
 
 
• **Affinity** (समानता): A natural liking for or attraction to a person, thing, idea, etc.
 
 
• **Example:** She has a natural affinity for languages.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.

Seema said to her daughter, "Don't go near the well."

options.text: Seema told her daughter that don't go near the well.
Seema said her daughter you shouldn't go near the well.
Seema requested to her daughter to go near the well.
Seema warned her daughter not to go near the well.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

As it is clear from the statement that statement is imperative we need to use the structure of imperative to change it into passive.

**Don't + main verb + object (direct)**

**Not + To + main verb + object (indirect)**

indirect structure is followed only by option 4 so it will be the right choice.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate passive form of the given sentence.

She answered fifty questions in one hour.

options.text: Fifty questions have been answered by her in one hour.
Fifty questions were answered by her in one hour.
Fifty questions are answered by her in one hour.
Fifty questions were being answered by her in one hour.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option is 2.

**Active voice - SUB + V2 + object + other word.**

**Passive voice - Object + was/ were + v3 + by + subject + other word.**

The passive structure is followed only by the option 2.

so this will be the correct choice.
